header.act: ACT VII — TO THE POLISH BORDER
player.speaker: Front Commissar
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.reaction-briliant.text: Kassa is taken. We are copying appeals in Slovak and sending them north by rail. My organisers speak openly of a Slovak republic. I remind them that ink and expectation are not yet a government.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.reaction-tactical.text: We took Kassa and very little else. Leaflets promise councils and a Slovak republic as though ink could hold the road to Eperjes. Unless the army opens that road, the proclamation remains a rumour.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.reaction-victory.text: Kassa is in our hands. Bundles of Slovak appeals are already moving north, and revolutionary committees are forming wherever the old officials have lost their nerve. No one yet agrees which committee has the right to speak for a new republic.
line.callback-kassa.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.callback-kassa.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-kassa.text: Kassa is ours, and the junction with it. Every train the Czechoslovak command wanted to move south now goes the long way or not at all.
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.callback-doctrine-rapid.text: At Kassa you chose pursuit over preparation. The junction fell before reinforcements arrived, and the mobile formations now treat every timetable as an insult. They are also further from their supply than the plan allowed for.
line.callback-doctrine-methodical.text: At Kassa you made us wait for guns and railway crews. Stromfeld has his supplied divisions; the enemy also had hours to recover. The argument is not settled by taking the city—it follows us onto the next road.
line.presov-printing-room.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.presov-printing-room.text: The Kassa presses have not stopped. Slovak on one forme, Hungarian on the next. Workers in Eperjes ask whether our red flags mean their councils or Budapest in a new colour. The battalions will answer before the leaflets do.
line.stromfeld-opening.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.stromfeld-opening.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.stromfeld-opening.text: The enemy fronts are separating. Bártfa would put us across their communications and near the Polish frontier. It is also the hardest point to supply. Every kilometre north needs ammunition—and a reason for the villages not to bar the road.
line.janousek-message.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.janousek-message.text: Workers in the occupied towns ask whether the Red Army has come to restore old Hungarian rule or to help them elect councils of their own. Forbid undisciplined requisition, publish orders in the local languages, and make the answer visible before nationalist officers provide one of their own.
line.landler-national-answer.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-national-answer.text: Many of these soldiers marched because Kassa was taken from Hungary, not because they had studied your programme. Tell them that every victory merely creates another state beyond Budapest and you may keep internationalism while losing the army that carried it north.
line.janousek-internationalist-reply.tex: Then tell them the truth: Hungarian workers cannot ask Slovak workers to reject Prague while obeying Budapest. If the councils mean only the old kingdom under red flags, the villages will resist us—and they will be right to doubt our proclamations.
line.landler-question.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-question.text: The political answer will be judged on roads that favour ambush and delay. Do we bind the advance to one disciplined railway axis, or let parallel columns reach more valleys at the cost of tighter control?
line.landler-question.choice.railway-axi: Drive the main force along the railway and seize each junction before the enemy can demolish it.
Gain a transport column, a larger prestige award and near-full core resupply, but forgo the parallel advance's core-wide experience.
line.landler-question.choice.parallel-co: Advance in parallel columns through the valleys so one roadblock cannot halt the whole operation.
Gain a prestige award and experience for every core formation, but forgo the transport column and near-full resupply.
line.stromfeld-railway.speaker: Aurél Stromfeld
line.stromfeld-railway.role: Chief of Staff, Hungarian Red Army
line.stromfeld-railway.text: The railway gives speed and supply, but it also makes our intention obvious. Keep flank detachments on the heights and engineers at the head of the column.
line.landler-columns.speaker: Jenő Landler
line.landler-columns.text: Parallel movement reduces the danger of a single roadblock, but the columns must remain within supporting distance. Do not let the terrain turn one army into three isolated detachments.
line.janousek-final.speaker: Antonín Janoušek
line.janousek-final.text: Take Bártfa and protect the villages from requisition without receipt or authority. Leave elected councils behind the columns. A Slovak republic proclaimed under bayonets alone will disappear when those bayonets move.
